profile.reading:
Per CoreSite's own facility page, this building, SV7, is located at 3020 Coronado Drive, Santa Clara, CA 95054, part of CoreSite's nine-building Silicon Valley campus. CoreSite publishes more than 227,000 square feet for this building. No MW capacity or opening year is stated. CoreSite lists SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, PCI DSS, and HIPAA compliance for its facilities generally.

CoreSite's Santa Clara sub-campus (SV3 through SV9) is described in a CoreSite construction-approval release as exceeding 775,000 square feet combined, part of a nine-building, 1.4-million-plus-square-foot Silicon Valley presence spanning San Jose, Santa Clara, and Milpitas. CoreSite is a subsidiary of American Tower Corporation (NYSE: AMT), which completed its acquisition of CoreSite in late 2021; Stonepeak Partners LP separately acquired roughly 29% of American Tower's US data center business in July 2022, later increased to about 36%. CoreSite's own site describes a total portfolio of 30 data centers across 11 US markets totaling more than 4.8 million square feet, with more than 44,000 customer interconnections and 500-plus connected network providers.

American Tower reported record leasing at CoreSite driving stronger-than-expected second-quarter 2026 results, projecting data-center segment revenue of $1.20 billion to $1.22 billion for full-year 2026, roughly 14.9% growth at the midpoint, and raising its full-year outlook on the strength of that performance; the company also budgeted approximately $695 million in data-center development spending for 2026, funding continued build-out across CoreSite's 11-market US portfolio.

Coronado Drive, where SV7 sits alongside SV3 and SV6, is the second major concentration point on CoreSite's Santa Clara campus, reflecting the same tight-cluster development pattern seen on the campus's Stender Way buildings, where operators favor shared infrastructure and short interconnection distances over a more dispersed footprint.

profile.research_note:
Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 34 (CoreSite missing-address campaign): added an operator-confirmed address and square footage, an aggregator up-to design MW figure recorded in capacity_note only. research_status remains complete.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] CoreSite was founded in 2001 as CRG West, a Carlyle Group portfolio company, beginning operations at two West Coast carrier hotel buildings, Market Post Tower and One Wilshire, both in Los Angeles. The firm rebranded from CRG West to CoreSite in June 2009 and completed an IPO in September 2010. American Tower Corporation, the public tower and infrastructure company (NYSE: AMT, SEC CIK 1053507), completed its acquisition of CoreSite in December 2021. Stonepeak Partners LP later bought roughly 29 percent of American Towers US data center business directly in July 2022, increasing that stake to about 36 percent by October 2022. CoreSites own current Silicon Valley regional page (operator source, tier-1, https://www.coresite.com/data-center-locations/silicon-valley) names nine data centers on this Santa Clara campus, SV1 through SV9, totaling more than 1.4 million square feet campus wide, but only describes SV1, SV2, SV4, SV7, SV8, and SV9 individually, SV1 and SV2 are not rows in this registry. SV3, SV5, and SV6 are not detailed on that page, so their building specific facts below come from data center industry aggregator directories instead. CoreSites own regional page gives this specific building, SV7, an address of 3020 Coronado Drive, Santa Clara, CA 95054, with 227,000 plus square feet, corroborated by Baxtel and DataCenterMap. Baxtel additionally describes this building as supporting up to 18 MW of critical IT load, a maximum design figure from an aggregator rather than a confirmed current operating figure published by the operator, so it is recorded in capacity_note only and not applied to critical_it_mw, consistent with this projects treatment of up-to and design-maximum figures elsewhere.

reading.body:
CoreSite SV7 is a 227,000-square-foot building on CoreSite's nine-building Santa Clara campus. The operator publishes no power capacity figure for this building. An industry aggregator reports a design maximum of 18 MW of critical IT load, which if achieved would translate to roughly 450 racks at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, though this is an unconfirmed design figure, not a current operating claim. The building holds SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, PCI DSS, and HIPAA certifications.

Santa Clara County hosts 103 mapped data center facilities, of which 11 publish power capacity totaling 365 MW. This campus ranks twelfth in the state by published capacity, meaning ten facilities with published figures exceed it. CoreSite's own Silicon Valley portfolio spans nine buildings totaling more than 1.4 million square feet across San Jose, Santa Clara, and Milpitas, with SV7 clustered alongside SV3 and SV6 on Coronado Drive, a pattern of tight co-location that reflects the industry preference for shared infrastructure and short interconnection distances.

CoreSite operates as a subsidiary of American Tower Corporation following its December 2021 acquisition. American Tower budgeted approximately $695 million in data-center development spending for 2026 across CoreSite's 11-market US portfolio and reported record leasing at CoreSite driving stronger-than-expected Q2 2026 results. Without a published MW figure for SV7 itself, the building's current role in meeting the grid constraint on AI scaling in California cannot be determined from operator disclosures.
